content: 1. Share a complete list of all the products you are using, including prescription and non-prescription medications, with your doctor and pharmacist. 2. Olsalazine is pharmacologically very similar to mesalamine. 3. This medication may interfere with certain laboratory tests, such as urine normetanephrine levels, potentially leading to inaccurate test results. 4. In the event of an overdose, if the individual exhibits severe symptoms such as loss of consciousness or difficulty breathing, immediately call emergency services (911). 5. If the situation is not life-threatening, contact a poison control center without delay. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222. 6. While taking this medication, laboratory and/or medical tests, such as kidney and liver function tests, may be conducted to monitor your health. 7. Ensure that you attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. 8. If you miss a dose, take it as soon as you remember. If it is close to the time of your next dose, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. 9. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. 10. Do not store this medication in the bathroom. 11. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. 12. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. 13.
